messages:
deploy-bot: [deploy] Started canary rollout for api-service @prod (10%) — version v1.12.3 — commit abc1234 by michael — CI: https://ci.redwood.internal/12345
ashley: wow, spike of 5xx right after that canary kicked off. dashboards.show -> errors up ~8% for /generate
ashley: paging SRE oncall, tagging here. @incident-bot please page @sre-oncall
incident-bot: Paging @sre-oncall — incident created: INC-2026-032-1792345678 (high error-rate on /generate). Join thread to coordinate.
priyanka: taking pager — looking now. can anyone confirm if it’s a specific instance or across canary?
michael: I see an unusual NPE in the model loader in the logs for 2 of the canary pods. stack: java.lang.NullPointerException at ModelBootstrap.init(ModelBootstrap.java:87)
priyanka: ok thx — isolating canary pods. ashley can you mute alerts on that rule for the next 15m (so we don't get paged repeatedly)?
ashley: muted alert rule prod-api-5xx for 15m :white_check_mark:
michael: theory: commit abc1234 tweaked kv-cache initialization. quick revert to be safe. planning immediate rollback of that commit from the canary.
priyanka: agree. michael, please revert in git and trigger canary redeploy. call out if you need help.
michael: performing revert now. steps: ```git revert --no-edit abc1234 && git push origin HEAD && ./deploy.sh api-service --canary 10```
deploy-bot: Received deploy request: api-service rollback -> creating new canary release (v1.12.2-rc-revert)
priyanka: I'll watch pod statuses and healthchecks. ashley, keep an eye on customer-facing metrics (latency / errors).
jake: noticed one support ticket referencing timeout on /generate around 14:12 UTC. told them we’re investigating.
michael: canary pods replaced — logs look clean so far. no more NPEs. rolling traffic will stay at 10% for 5m, then increase if stable.
ashley: error rate trending down — back to baseline ~0.5% in last 2m :thumbsup:
priyanka: nice. keeping this as an active incident until we confirm no regression across regions. what's impact window and estimated user-facing impact?
michael: preliminary: affected only canary cohort ~10% of requests; estimate ~2% of total requests experienced errors for ~4 minutes. no SLO breaches flagged yet.
jake: support: replied to the ticket, offered status update, no escalations. will follow up if more reports.
priyanka: good. creating short incident note: cause = bad kv-cache init in abc1234, mitigation = quick revert of commit and canary redeploy. owner = michael. action items: postmortem (michael + priyanka), add unit test for kv-cache init, improve canary health gating.
jess: (next on-call) I'll take handoff at 18:00 UTC, ping me with current incident state.
priyanka: handing off to jess for overnight monitoring. current status: stable, no errors in last 6m, canary at 10% pending full rollout hold. please escalate to paging if error rate rises above 1% for 5m.
incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-032-1792345678 marked RESOLVED by priyanka — duration 00:10:20 — summary: reverted bad commit, canary stable.
michael: will open postmortem doc and link here: https://docs.redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2026-032-postmortem
ashley: adding a short note to status page to proactively notify any customers who reported timeouts.
priyanka: thanks all — great quick coordination. closing thread after handoff. :white_check_mark:
